message: `in shared` is only permitted in a `function` parameter list, not in a `constructor` parameter list

`in shared` is only permitted on an `external` function: a shared handle is an ABI wire type, and an internal call site is not rewritten, so a `public` function's own internal callers could not pass one

`in shared` is only permitted on an `external` function: a shared handle is an ABI wire type, and an internal call site is not rewritten, so a `public` function's own internal callers could not pass one
`in shared` is not permitted on a `view` or `pure` function: receiving a shared handle changes the access-control state
this parameter list mixes `in shared` inputs with external `in` inputs; a function may declare either kind, not both (split it into two functions)
`in shared` takes no proof binder: a shared handle is received from its sharer, not verified against an input proof
a recipient belongs on a shared *return* type; an input is written `in shared eT name` with no recipient
`in shared` must be followed by an encrypted type (ebool, euint8..euint128, eaddress)
a shared-boundary declaration takes no data location: `calldata` has no meaning on an encrypted value type (remove it)
`in shared` is only permitted in a `function` parameter list, not in a `modifier` parameter list
a shared return must be unnamed: the value is wrapped where it is returned, so a named fallthrough return has nothing to wrap
a shared return must be the only return of its function: this list declares more than one return value
the only recipient this version accepts is `msg.sender`; the transpiler cannot prove another expression names the caller
a shared return is not permitted on a `view` or `pure` function: sharing a handle changes the access-control state
a shared return is only permitted on a `public` or `external` function: a shared handle is an ABI wire type, so an internal caller has nothing to receive
`shared(...)` must be followed by an encrypted type (ebool, euint8..euint128, eaddress)
a function with a shared return must return a value explicitly: `return <expr>;`
a `return` of a shared value must sit inside a braced block: wrap the branch body in `{ }`
the returned expression of a shared return must not assign: assign in its own statement and return the variable
a shared-boundary declaration takes no data location: `memory` has no meaning on an encrypted value type (remove it)
a shared-boundary marker is only permitted on a function parameter (`in shared eT name`) or on a function return type (`shared(msg.sender) eT`), not in an error parameter list
